title: Absolute ampleness after twisting a relatively ample invertible module
statement: Let $f:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume that $f$ is quasi-compact (the inverse image of each affine open is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), that $N|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq T$, and that $M$ is ample on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there is an integer $a_0\geq0$ such that for every integer $a\geq a_0$, the invertible module $N\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z} f^*(M^{\otimes a})$ is ample on $Z$. Here $f^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the tensor products and tensor powers use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Put $P_a=N\otimes f^*(M^{\otimes a})$ for $a\geq0$. The tensor and pullback assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] show that these are invertible and identify their powers by $P_a^{\otimes n}\cong N^{\otimes n}\otimes f^*(M^{\otimes an})$, compatibly with sections and their fibre values. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $T$ is quasi-compact; hence $Z$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). The ample module $M$ makes $T$ separated by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated], so $V\cap V'$ is affine for affine opens $V,V'\subseteq T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] with $A=\mathbf Z$. For affine $V\subseteq T$, $Z_V=f^{-1}(V)$ carries the ample module $N|_{Z_V}$, so it is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated] and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Cover $Z$ by the affine opens $U$ lying in some $Z_V$ with $V$ affine. Take $U\subseteq Z_V$, $U'\subseteq Z_{V'}$ and put $V''=V\cap V'$, so $U\cap U'\subseteq Z_{V''}$. As $U$ is quasi-compact and $V$ quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $U\to V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1); so $U\cap Z_{V''}$, the inverse image of the affine $V''$, is quasi-compact, and likewise $U'\cap Z_{V''}$. Cover both by finitely many affine opens of $Z_{V''}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](1) on $Z_{V''}$ their pairwise intersections are quasi-compact, so $U\cap U'$ is quasi-compact. Part (2) of that lemma makes $Z$ quasi-separated, and part (1) makes intersections of affine opens of $Z$ quasi-compact. These are exactly the hypotheses needed for clearing denominators below.

Fix $z\in Z$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] applied to $M$ supplies $m\geq1$ and $t\in\Gamma(T,M^{\otimes m})$ with $f(z)\in T_t$ and $T_t$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-power-section-nonvanishing-pullback] there is a section $q$ of $(f^*M)^{\otimes m}\cong f^*(M^{\otimes m})$ with $Z_q=f^{-1}(T_t)$. This last module identification is given by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. The assumption on $N$ applies to the affine open $T_t$. Applying the same ampleness definition on $U=Z_q$ gives $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(U,N^{\otimes n}|_U)$ such that $W=U_s$ is affine and contains $z$. Thus $W$ has been chosen independently of the eventual twisting exponent.

The module $N^{\otimes n}$ is invertible by induction using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1); it is therefore quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply [lem-sc-p1-section-clearing-denominators-qcqs] on the quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $Z$ to the invertible module $f^*(M^{\otimes m})$, its section $q$, and the quasi-coherent module $N^{\otimes n}$. There exist $e\geq0$ and $s'\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n}\otimes f^*(M^{\otimes em}))$ whose restriction to $U=Z_q$ is $s q^e$. For every $b>0$, multiplication gives $s'q^b$ in $\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n}\otimes f^*(M^{\otimes(e+b)m}))$. Its nonvanishing locus is exactly $W$: outside $U$, the factor $q^b$ has zero fibre value; inside $U$, $q$ is a nonzero vector in a one-dimensional fibre, so $s'q^b=sq^{e+b}$ is nonzero exactly where $s$ is nonzero. The tensor fibre-value formula used here is [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3).

For every integer $a$ divisible by $m$ with $a\geq m(e+1)$, put $b=na/m-e$. Then $b\geq1$ and $(e+b)m=na$. The section just constructed is consequently a section of $P_a^{\otimes n}$ whose affine nonvanishing locus is the fixed $W$. Do this for every $z$. Quasi-compactness of $Z$ allows finitely many of these $W_i$ to cover it. Let $D$ be a positive common multiple of their $m_i$ and choose a nonnegative multiple $A$ of $D$ with $A\geq m_i(e_i+1)$ for every $i$. Every $W_i$ is an affine nonvanishing locus of a section of a positive power of $P_A$; by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $P_A$ is ample. If $Z$ is empty, its quasi-compactness and the vacuous point condition already show every $P_a$ ample, so take $a_0=0$ and finish. Thus the finite cover in the nonempty case has at least one member.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] on $T$ with the ample module $M$ and the finite type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal O_T$. The latter hypotheses follow directly from [pqf-def-coherent]: on an affine chart it is the associated module of the ring itself, and the identity is a rank-one local finite generating map. It follows that there is $K\geq0$ such that $M^{\otimes c}$ is generated by finitely many global sections for all $c\geq K$. The identification $\mathcal O_T\otimes M^{\otimes c}\cong M^{\otimes c}$ is the tensor-unit identification. By [lem-sc-global-generation-nonvanishing-cover], for each such $c$ the nonvanishing loci $T_v$ of global sections $v$ of $M^{\otimes c}$ cover $T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-power-section-nonvanishing-pullback] to the invertible module $M^{\otimes c}$ and tensor degree $1$. Their pulled-back sections $w$ of $Q_c=f^*(M^{\otimes c})$ have loci $Z_w=f^{-1}(T_v)$, which cover $Z$.

Set $a_0=A+K$ and fix $a\geq a_0$, so $c=a-A\geq K$. For $z\in Z$, ampleness of $P_A$ gives $r\geq1$ and $u\in\Gamma(Z,P_A^{\otimes r})$ with $z\in Z_u$ and $Z_u$ affine, by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Choose a section $w$ of $Q_c$ nonvanishing at $z$ from the preceding cover. Then $u\otimes w^{\otimes r}$ is a section of $(P_A\otimes Q_c)^{\otimes r}$ with locus $Z_u\cap Z_w$, by the fibre-value formula of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3). This intersection is affine by [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open], applied to the affine open $Z_u$ and the invertible module $Q_c$. It contains $z$. The ampleness definition now proves $P_A\otimes Q_c$ ample. The pullback tensor isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2), with the tensor-power regrouping, identifies this module with $P_{A+c}=P_a$. Apply [lem-sc-ample-iso] to conclude that $P_a$ is ample. Since $a$ was arbitrary, this proves the stated uniform tail.
